---
title: "Create Your First Feature"
sidebarTitle: "Get Started"
description: "Connect an application, configure its delivery context, and submit a focused Build request that produces a reviewable pull request."
---


This guide takes you from a fresh workspace to a first generated feature.

<CardGroup cols={3}>
  <Card title="Time to complete" icon="clock">
    Plan for 10 to 15 minutes if your repository access is ready.
  </Card>
  <Card title="What you need" icon="git-branch">
    A repository Revolte can read, write to, and open pull requests against.
  </Card>
  <Card title="What you receive" icon="git-pull-request">
    A scoped pull request with implementation notes, validation context, and tests where appropriate.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

<Note>
  <strong>Repository access</strong>
  <br />
  You need access to the target Git repository and permission to connect it to Revolte.
</Note>

<Tip>
  <strong>Need the product overview first?</strong>
  <br />
  Read [Introduction to Revolte](/docs) to understand the full platform in 2 to 5 minutes.
</Tip>

## Before you start

Prepare these details before opening the setup flow:

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Repository access" icon="lock-keyhole">
    Confirm that Revolte can access the repository and create branches or pull requests.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Target branch" icon="git-commit">
    Know where generated pull requests should be opened, usually your main development branch.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Application context" icon="app-window">
    Know the app name, framework, runtime, and any important build or test commands.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Delivery expectations" icon="list-checks">
    Decide which environments, preview flows, and deployment checks matter for the first build.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## Connect Your Application

Complete the guided setup before submitting your first Build request. This gives Revolte the workspace, repository, project, application, and workflow context it needs to generate code safely.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Sign up">
    [Create your Revolte account](https://console.revolte.ai/auth/login) and open the onboarding flow.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Complete workspace details">
    Add your organization details and role so Revolte can tailor the workspace context.

    ![Workspace details modal for entering organization name, role, and referral source](/images/quickstart/quick-start-1.png)
  </Step>

  <Step title="Select a cloud target">
    Choose where Revolte should run and manage the application infrastructure.

    ![Cloud target selection with Revolte Cloud selected](/images/quickstart/quick-start-2.png)

  </Step>

  <Step title="Connect source control">
    Connect the Git provider that contains the repository Revolte should use for generated work.

    ![Source control integration options with GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and custom token fields](/images/quickstart/quick-start-3.png)
  </Step>

  <Step title="Connect project management">
    Optionally connect a product management tool so issues or requirements can be linked to build workflows.

    ![Project management integration step with Jira selected](/images/quickstart/quick-start-4.png)
  </Step>

  <Step title="Create the project">
    Create or select the project that groups related applications under the same product context.

    ![Project creation form with project name and Jira project mapping](/images/quickstart/quick-start-5.png)
  </Step>

  <Step title="Create the application">
    Name the application and select the repository Revolte should manage.

    ![Application creation form with application name and repository selection](/images/quickstart/quick-start-6.png)
  </Step>

  <Step title="Configure the YAML">
    Review the generated `revolte.yml`, framework selection, branch mapping, workflow toggles, and validation settings.

    ![Pipeline configuration screen showing framework, branch mapping, workflow toggles, and generated YAML](/images/quickstart/quick-start-7.png)

  </Step>

  <Step title="Launch the application">
    Confirm the launch checklist and let Revolte initialize the application workflow.

    ![Launch confirmation checklist over generated Revolte configuration](/images/quickstart/quick-start-8.png)
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Configure Advanced Workflows (Optional)

You can customize how Revolte handles code reviews, linting, and testing through the **YAML Configuration** in your application settings.

- [Pre-Build Workflows](/docs/build/pre-build-workflows): Set up automated code review and summarization.
- [Validation Pipeline](/docs/build/validation-pipeline): Enable automated linting and test suite execution.


## Write a strong requirement

A good Build request tells Revolte what should be true after the change lands.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Good">
    ```txt
    Add JWT authentication to the user profile API.

    Require a valid bearer token, return 401 for missing or invalid tokens,
    preserve the existing response shape, and add tests for success, missing
    token, and expired token cases.
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Too vague">
    ```txt
    Add auth.
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Use this checklist when writing your first request:

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Define the behavior" icon="target">
    Describe what should happen from the user's or API consumer's point of view.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Name inputs and outputs" icon="braces">
    Include request fields, response shape, UI states, files, or commands that matter.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Call out constraints" icon="shield-check">
    Mention authentication, permissions, framework patterns, and compatibility requirements.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Ask for validation" icon="test-tube">
    Tell Revolte which tests or checks should prove the change works.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>


<Note>
  Review the generated pull request before merging. Revolte accelerates implementation, but your team's review standards still apply.
</Note>
